newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Ayala Corp 96 net profits up, 97 seen higher.
newsitem.headline: Ayala Corp 96 net profits up, 97 seen higher.

text.p: The Philippines oldest conglomerate, Ayala Corp, posted 6.23 billion pesos ($237 million) 1996 profits, up 14 percent from 1995 and analysts said double-digit earnings growth may be repeated this year.

But the 1997 performance would hinge on improvements in its telecom and food units, along with continued strength in its property and banking units, analysts said on Friday after Ayala announced its results.
A Reuters poll of five securities firms in January had forecast Ayala net profit in 1996 at 5.56 billion pesos. In 1995, the company posted a net income of 5.48 billion pesos.
Stripped of extra-ordinary gains, 1995 income was at 4.18 billion.

Ayala Corp, which began as a distillery in 1834, has interests in property through Ayala Land Inc, banking through Bank of the Philippine Islands, insurance with Ayala Life Assurance Inc, food via Pure Foods Inc, electronics through Integrated Microelectronics Inc and telecommunications with Globe Telecom GMCR Inc
Of its subsidiaries, Ayala Land and BPI Corp each posted four billion peso net income in 1996.
Ayala Life made 451 million pesos, Integrated Microelectronics made 241 million pesos and Pure Foods made 21 million pesos.
The only unit to register a loss was cellular phone operator Globe with a 750 million peso shortfall.
"Ayala Corp's growth was above our expectations but we were expecting more from Ayala Land," said Noel Reyes, research head at Anscor Hagedorn Securities Inc.
Reyes said some projects of Ayala Land expected to be booked in 1996 may possibly be factored in this year, resulting in lower earnings for the property counter than projected.

"We were looking at lower losses of Globe, somewhere at 500 million pesos last year. I think growth in 1997 will come from minimised losses in Globe Telecom as well as improvement in Pure Foods," said Gio de la Rosa, analyst at ING Baring Securities.
Globe's service area, which includes the lucrative Makati City, is expected to generate substantial earnings this year, All Asia Securities research head Helen Alvarez said.
Fraudulent calls led to Globe's losses in 1996 but the firm has now set up anti-fraud measures.
Ayala Corp said a poultry supply glut in 1996 adversely affected Pure Foods financial performance despite its leadership in the meats and flour milling businesses.
"Earnings growth of Ayala Corp will be sustainable, especially with Ayala Land's expansion into areas outside Metro Manila and BPI's merger with CityTrust Banking Corp," Anscor's Reyes added.
The merger of BPI and CityTrust took effect in 1996, making BPI the biggest in the consumer finance business.
Ayala Land, which owns 40 percent of the Makati business district, accounts for 60 percent of Ayala Corp's net income.

"We still see double-digit growth levels for Ayala Land's profits this year but it has to continue tapping other growth centres in view of the overheated property market in Metro Manila," said Alvarez at All Asia.

Last month, Ayala Corp president Jaime Augusto Zobel de Ayala told Reuters he saw no downturn in Manila property values, despite analysts' predictions of a slowdown after three years of a property boom. ($1 = 26.30 pesos)
